since.note: Threats are matched by element, category and title first (an element by its name, so a renumbered component is the same element). What is left is paired when the two threats cite nearly the same place in the code and agree on other signs (the same weakness id, category or words in the title); those pairs are listed as probably the same, with what they have in common, and are never counted as unchanged. Last, a threat with the same id as one in the other run is paired when its element and category agree. A threat the agent renamed and renumbered, with nothing else in common, shows as one removed and one added. This compares what two runs reported; it does not say which is right.

red_team_agent_objective.coverage_line: Covered by the agent: 5 of 8 categories claimed, 1 with a logged request, 1 skipped, 1 not applicable, 1 with a tool unavailable.

stride.name: Spoofing
stride.question: Can something pretend to be this element, or to be a caller of it?

stride.name: Tampering
stride.question: Can data or code here be changed without the owner knowing?

stride.name: Repudiation
stride.question: Can someone do something here and later deny it, because nothing records it?

stride.name: Information disclosure
stride.question: Can data reach someone who should not see it?

stride.name: Denial of service
stride.question: Can someone make this element unavailable or exhaust it?

stride.name: Elevation of privilege
stride.question: Can someone do more here than they are allowed to?

linddun.name: Linkability
linddun.question: Can two records or actions be tied to the same person?

linddun.name: Identifiability
linddun.question: Can a person be singled out from this data?

linddun.name: Non-repudiation
linddun.question: Is a person unable to deny something they would want to deny?

linddun.name: Detectability
linddun.question: Can someone tell that a record about a person exists?

linddun.name: Disclosure of information
linddun.question: Can personal data reach someone who should not have it?

linddun.name: Unawareness
linddun.question: Is the person unaware of what is collected or why?

linddun.name: Non-compliance
linddun.question: Does the handling miss a rule, policy or consent it should follow?

wstg.title: Information gathering
wstg.intent: What the target reveals about itself: versions, routes, files and metadata a visitor can read.

wstg.title: Configuration and deployment
wstg.intent: Default settings, exposed admin or debug interfaces, missing security headers and risky methods.

wstg.title: Authentication
wstg.intent: Whether signing in can be bypassed, guessed or worn down, and how credentials are reset.

wstg.title: Authorization
wstg.intent: Whether one user can reach another user's data or a higher role's functions.

wstg.title: Session management
wstg.intent: How session tokens are made, kept, expired and protected, and whether cross-site requests are stopped.

wstg.title: Input validation
wstg.intent: Whether data the caller controls can change a query, a command, a file path, a template or an outbound request.

wstg.title: Client side
wstg.intent: Script injection, unsafe redirects, framing and cross-origin settings in what the browser receives.

wstg.title: API
wstg.intent: Object and function level access, mass assignment, rate limits and schema handling on the API routes.
